critique.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_action: The geometry-to-waypoint connection needed a more concrete calibrated fitting procedure for the small visible top face. For the container identified at front pixel [95,97], jointly reconstruct corresponding physical top corners in the current front and wrist views, rather than approximate its centre and yaw from image appearance. The required reconstruction gives an approach centre near world x=-0.0097, y=-0.1174 and square-edge yaw=0.2971; my estimate displaced the centre by about 1.14 cm. Identity, approach height, and gripper state were already specified correctly.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action:
At the initial open-hand approach for a requested green cube, the demonstration had moved its covering container to the left side of the front image. Memory correctly identified that container by its final silhouette centre and preserved the settled demonstration frame. The policy selected the right container, approach height, and open gripper, but its estimated horizontal centre missed the recorded approach by slightly more than 1 cm. This is a SUFFICIENCY failure in the geometry-to-waypoint instruction, not an identity or memory-transition failure.

Strengthen the existing top-face reconstruction rule with a concrete two-view fitting procedure. When both calibrated current cameras show the stationary selected container, match its physical top-face corners between the front and wrist images before estimating the approach centre. Distinguish top-face boundaries from lower silhouette edges and shaded side faces. Parameterize the top as a horizontal square with unknown centre (x,y,h), side length s, and world yaw theta: its four corners are (x,y,h) plus the yaw-rotated offsets (±s/2,±s/2,0). Project those same four world corners through each camera's supplied calibration and jointly fit the parameters to the observed corresponding corners and physical edges. Resolve corner-order ambiguity by testing cyclic correspondences and retaining the fit consistent with both views and the visible side faces. Use all usable corners rather than estimating the centre or yaw from the small front-image face alone. If a corner is occluded or clipped, constrain it by the fitted square and visible edges; do not substitute an image boundary. Check the fitted projections against both images before accepting the centre. Use the fitted x,y for the open approach at z=0.20 m and derive yaw from the fitted world edges, choosing the square-equivalent orientation nearest the current hand orientation. Refine the same geometry before the closing descent. Retain the existing stationary-reference fallback when current observations are unusable, and retain all existing identity, lift-count, grasp, return, and withdrawal rules. No episode-specific coordinates or additional memory fields are needed.

fields.name: target_locations
fields.description: During the video cycle, identify which container descends over each requested cube colour. Follow those containers continuously across the shuffle frames, including exchanges between identical-looking containers. Write their final front-image silhouette centres as [u,v] pixel pairs in requested colour order. Do not infer identity from the final arrangement alone or assume a container returned to its original identity because the arrangement repeats. Carry this list unchanged at every act cycle. e.g. [[131,71],[117,146]]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of [u,v] front-image container-centre locations, in pixels, at the end of the demonstration, one for each requested cube colour in instruction order. Identify the container that originally covered each requested cube and follow its continuous motion through every shuffle; record its final location, not the cube's original location. Include no distractors. Use the centre of the entire visible container silhouette consistently. Set this list at the video cycle and retain it throughout execution, including after a selected container moves. e.g. [[131,71],[117,146]]

fields.name: completed_lifts
fields.description: Initialize to zero at the video cycle. Increment once when this cycle's motion frames show the next requested container rising with the closed gripper from grasp height to approximately 0.20 m TCP height. The container must move with the hand; a newly exposed cube supports confirmation. Count the observed lift, not a lift you are about to command. Do not increment for a static elevated grasp, a downward return, an open-hand withdrawal, or a grasp closure at low height. If the motion executes no steps, retain the count. Otherwise retain the incoming value unless this successful new lift is observed. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Number of requested containers already lifted successfully in instruction order. Initialize to zero at the video cycle. Increment at the first act cycle showing the selected container carried upward from grasp height to approximately 0.20 m TCP height with the gripper closed. Do not increment for closing at grasp height, returning a container, withdrawing with an open gripper, or continuing to hold an already-counted container. Retain the count otherwise. e.g. 1

fields.name: final_layout_keyframe
fields.description: During the video cycle, select the last shown frame of the settled final arrangement in which the requested containers are unobstructed and write its frame label. Carry that label unchanged at every act cycle. Do not replace it with an execution frame or update it when a completed container is returned. Its geometry is a reference only for containers that have not subsequently moved. e.g. V113
fields.annotation: The label of the last shown demonstration frame of the settled final arrangement in which the requested containers are unobstructed. Set at the video cycle and retain unchanged throughout execution, including after a selected container is returned. This frame preserves reference geometry for targets that have not subsequently moved, not the current pose of returned containers. e.g. V113

texts.action:
At the video cycle output memory only. Execution starts with an open hand above the scene and completed_lifts equal to zero. Use target_locations to identify the requested containers in the current front image; the list records identities by their final demonstration locations, not their initial cube locations. Distinguish container identity from grasp geometry. target_locations stores whole-silhouette image centres for identifying containers, not projections of their grasp axes at a known height. Identify the selected container using target_locations, then locate its physical top-face corners using usable calibrated observations. For an unfinished target that has not moved since the demonstration, use final_layout_keyframe as an unobstructed reference whenever current views hide or truncate its physical top corners. Match the reference container using target_locations, without treating the stored silhouette centre as a grasp-axis projection. Use the current wrist view to refine that same container, not to switch to a nearby one. If the target is outside the wrist view or supplies no usable wrist geometry, use its stationary reference geometry rather than forcing a wrist-based estimate. In clipped views, infer missing physical corners from visible physical edges and square constraints; neither the image boundary nor the centroid of the visible fragment defines the container geometry. Recover the horizontal top-plane height and grasp centre by fitting consistent container geometry to usable calibrated observations. When both current cameras show the selected stationary container, match its physical top-face corners between the front and wrist images, distinguishing top boundaries from lower silhouette edges and shaded side faces. Parameterize the top as a horizontal square with centre (x,y,h), side length s, and world yaw theta; its corners are (x,y,h) plus yaw-rotated offsets (±s/2,±s/2,0). Project these same world corners through each camera's supplied calibration and jointly fit the parameters to all usable corresponding corners and physical edges. Test cyclic corner correspondences and retain the fit consistent with both views and the visible vertical side faces. Constrain occluded or clipped corners with the fitted square and visible physical edges, never with an image boundary. Check the fitted projections against both images before accepting the centre; do not estimate geometry from the small front-image top face alone when usable wrist observations exist. When current observations are unusable or incomplete, retain the stationary-reference fallback above, fitting the square top and vertical sides to the reference front view together with any usable current observations. Do not use demonstration geometry as the current pose of a container that has subsequently moved. Do not choose an arbitrary plane height or project the silhouette centre onto the table. For world-to-camera calibration R,t, the camera centre is C=-R^T t and the world ray through pixel [u,v] is d=R^T K^-1[u,v,1]. Its intersection with a top plane of height h is C+((h-C_z)/d_z)d. Reconstruct the physical top corners on this plane and average their world coordinates to obtain the grasp-axis x,y centre. Determine yaw from the fitted or reconstructed world-plane square edges, not raw image-edge angles, choosing the square-equivalent orientation nearest the current hand orientation. Use this recovered x,y for both the open approach at z=0.20 m and the closing descent at z=0.0633 m, refining it with current imagery before descent. Robot-left is +y, which appears on the right of the front image. Grasp the container, not the cube.

Apply the following rules to the observed state, accounting for a lift observed in this cycle before selecting the action. With an empty open hand and an unfinished target, select target_locations[completed_lifts]. If not already above that container at approximately z=0.20 m, move to its world centre at z=0.20 m with the gripper open. Point straight down, roll=3.1416 and pitch=0, and align yaw with the container's opposing square sides. Infer the container centre independently of the reported TCP: long motions can stop roughly a centimetre short.

With the open hand above the selected container at approximately z=0.20 m, descend to the independently reconstructed grasp-axis centre at z=0.0633 m and close the gripper. Refine that centre from the current calibrated wrist and front imagery using the top-face reconstruction above. A small approach-motion error does not require another approach waypoint: correct x,y during descent. Neither the reported TCP x,y nor an assumed-height projection of the whole-silhouette centre substitutes for the reconstructed target centre. With the closed fingers around the container at this low height, raise its centre vertically to z=0.20 m, maintaining yaw and keeping the gripper closed. Fingers separated approximately 0.018 m each and a container between them indicate a grasp; do not release at this stage.

When a successful lift has just been observed and another requested target remains, return the held container before approaching the next one: keep the current TCP x,y and orientation, lower to z=0.070 m, and open at arrival. When the hand is open at this low return height, withdraw vertically at the current x,y to approximately z=0.147 m, remaining open. With the open hand at this withdrawal height, approach the next target at z=0.20 m. Do not regrasp the returned container merely because it is beneath the hand. completed_lifts distinguishes that completed target from the next requested one.

When the last requested container is grasped, lift it to z=0.20 m with the gripper closed; no return or extra container is required. If another cycle occurs after all requested lifts are confirmed, keep holding and wait briefly for termination.

For an unmatched or uncertain state, preserve the stored identities and completion count. Use the current wrist and front views to recover alignment. If empty and too low for safe lateral travel, withdraw vertically with the gripper open before approaching the unfinished target. If a grasp visibly failed, reopen while moving at least 5 mm, then realign and retry the same target without incrementing completed_lifts. Never issue an identical-pose waypoint; use a wait when only observation is needed.
